n6988464016.story: On the 18th floor of the south City Gate tower, with views over Herăstrău, Casa Presei and Kiseleff: 180 seats inside and 60 on the terrace. Since 2025 it has been run by the owners of Nor in Sky Tower.
n6988464016.crowd: evenings, at sunset, on the terrace; daily lunch menu 12–15

n3414081989.story: The bar opened in 2006 by Vlad Gorneanu, frontman of the band ZOB, on Covaci: rebel spirit, handmade decor, live music and conversations until late.
n3414081989.crowd: every day, until 3 am; busiest at weekends

n11638271659.story: A pub for geeks on Mendeleev: bring your own game or pick from their board game collection, with friendly people and a relaxed vibe.
n11638271659.crowd: evenings, with friends, for a board game night

n2507541755.story: Escape room in the centre, on I. L. Caragiale street: you have 60 minutes to solve the puzzles and get out of the room with your crew.

n13324821915.story: International restaurant at Biruinței 81, rated 4.8 from 37 votes on ialoc.

n6943415085.story: Wine bar on Tonitza street, at the edge of Centrul Vechi (Old Town), with a terrace and wine by the glass; open daily until 1 am.

n11064463050.story: Squash, padel and badminton courts on Bulevardul Mărăști, good to book with friends after work.

n5433115598.story: Lebanese food with mezze and lamb, plus hummus, falafel, Lebanese pies and shawarma. It's in AFI Cotroceni, on the edge of Drumul Taberei.
n5433115598.crowd: daily 9:30–21:30; after shopping or a movie

n2382674377.story: Arabic food and shawarma on Mihai Bravu, recommended among the good, cheap spots.

n12362055781.story: Café at Biruinței 87 with good coffee and cakes, also hosting book clubs, events and live music nights.

n11669695269.story: The only pizzeria in Romania in the Top 50 Pizza Europe: Neapolitan pizza with puffy crusts, on Visarion street.

n7622689033.story: The City Hall's cultural centre hosts exhibitions, concerts and shows in Hanul Gabroveni, an old inn in Centrul Vechi (Old Town) restored as an art space.

r4871608.story: The amphitheatre in Parcul Carol that hosts open-air summer concerts: in 2026 Empire of the Sun, KALEO, Skillet and Rita Ora played here. Without a concert it's closed, so check the schedule first.

n10199556329.story: Small, intimate Italian restaurant in Pipera, with ingredients brought from Italy; the praise goes to the pizza, pasta and tiramisu.

n9405774196.story: Rooftop on top of the National Theatre, with a 1,200 m² terrace and views over Bulevardul Magheru and the centre; it also has a covered area, so it works in any season.

n12368291207.story: Real Neapolitan pizza with biga dough, ranked first in Popești-Leordeni on TripAdvisor.

n5898763785.story: Brunch and coffee on Calea Victoriei, close to Centrul Vechi (Old Town).

n14058359290.story: Sweet and savoury tarts, on Ion Mihalache.

w16291602.story: Home of the "George Enescu" Philharmonic, opened in 1888; in the main hall, above the audience, a fresco about 75 m long tells the history of the Romanians.

n4957277421.story: Mediterranean restaurant on Smârdan street, a quieter corner of Centrul Vechi (Old Town).

n2387663653.story: Striking design with big windows and brunch for every taste, from vegetarian to burgers and American pancakes.

n14058623131.story: New café (summer 2026) on Ion Mihalache, with a shaded terrace.

w264742966.story: Neighbourhood Italian restaurant in Drumul Taberei, towards Militari (Valea Oltului 61): pizza, pasta, fish, salads and grilled dishes.

w858609086.story: One of the few pools in Bucharest where you can swim without being a competitive athlete; free swimming requires a pass (250 lei / 8 sessions).

n12765679610.story: The outdoor pool at the Dinamo Complex reopened to the public from 15 June; free swimming requires a pass (from 130 lei).

n5898775985.story: In Palatul Universul, one of the most laptop-friendly spots in town: stable wifi, lots of space, consistent coffee.

w954952572.story: Small bohemian bar on Calea Plevnei, with graffiti walls, a concert room and a garden: jazz nights and jam sessions where anyone can get on stage.
w954952572.crowd: on jazz or jam session nights (check their page)

n3807892722.story: Small restaurant that feels like a living room, on Mihai Eminescu, with a short menu that changes with the seasons.

w28230560.story: The largest beer hall in south-eastern Europe, with a terrace on the shore of Lake Herăstrău and concerts almost every weekend, from lăutari folk bands to Carla’s Dreams.

r18184396.story: Sector 4's new indoor ice rink, with public skating sessions and hockey games.

n6917823021.story: Turkish restaurant at Colentina 442, known for its grill: Adana kebab, chicken skewers, pide; 43–110 lei per person, with outdoor seating too.

w1490427698.story: The Turkish restaurant in Floreasca that became a legend for grilled kebab, pide and big portions.

w943937960.story: Restaurant with a terrace right on the shore of Lake Herăstrău, good for sunsets and dinner outdoors in summer.

n8911907337.story: Bouldering gym (climbing without ropes, on low walls above thick mats) where you can come even as a beginner.

n2533820134.story: Diner-style restaurant on Povernei, with flavours from Mexico, Brazil and Argentina: tacos, burritos and margaritas.

n5898729286.story: One of the original names in Bucharest specialty coffee, in Piața Charles de Gaulle.

n8599551539.story: Specialty coffee shop in the Dristor–Decebal area.

n11795216443.story: Specialty coffee and brunch, featured in the 2025 brunch guides.

n6929956290.story: French-style bakery and patisserie: croissants, bread and tarts, close to Calea Victoriei.

n11215700346.story: Brunch, good bread and coffee, just off Calea Victoriei.

n13544497939.story: Brunch with eggs every which way, near Piața Amzei.

n3096282348.story: One of the first good burger places in town, between Calea Victoriei and Cișmigiu, with a neighbourhood feel.

w232502551.story: Made its name with good ingredients, well-thought-out recipes and flawless execution, on Știrbei Vodă.

n5520224021.story: Canteen with Romanian food cooked fresh that day, at Mihail Sebastian 18.

c-calea-victoriei-pietonala-strazi-desch.story: From April to October, at weekends, Calea Victoriei closes to cars between Bd. Dacia and the Splai and becomes a promenade with workshops, parades, sport and music; since 2026 Ion Brezoianu street has been added too. Walk past the Athenaeum and Cercul Militar without dodging cars.
c-calea-victoriei-pietonala-strazi-desch.crowd: Saturday and Sunday, 10:00–22:00, from 25 April to 11 October 2026 (some weekends Saturday only)

n2611043627.story: Lebanese-style falafel and shawarma, in the Iancului area.

c-calul-balan-malul-lacului-buftea.story: Calul Bălan is a restaurant with a terrace on the shore of Lake Buftea, with a story going back to the '60s, and the spot where locals set off for a walk along the dam, past the church, to the back of Domeniul Știrbey. Summer evenings and weekends it's packed, and the hall often hosts weddings, so call ahead for the terrace.

w1235220017.story: Opened in 2025 on Constantin Aricescu, in Floreasca, one of the new spots "with Romanian stories" in last year's guides.

n3798121589.story: Small, welcoming café on Mendeleev, near Piața Amzei, good for a chat or for reading.

n13869497589.story: Sicilian cannoli with ricotta, in Floreasca.

w1234985989.story: Sicilian cannoli with ricotta, on Bulevardul Decebal.

n3487492200.story: Climbing and bouldering gym on Splaiul Independenței, with routes for beginners and advanced climbers.

n916075216.story: The beer hall founded in 1879 has been in the neo-Gothic building on Stavropoleos since 1899, with stained glass, vaults and painted walls. Order mici, pork knuckle and the house beer.
n916075216.crowd: anytime; fills up in the evening, book ahead

n4548618789.story: Restaurant with a garden at Novaci 9B (13 Septembrie), with tripe soup, sarmale with polenta and papanași; 4.0 from over 1,300 Google reviews.

n8974886497.story: The second Casa de Tacos, at Calea Victoriei 214: the same tacos from recipes brought back from a trip to Mexico.

n10038019966.story: Small spot hidden in an alley behind Unirea Shopping Center, started out of a passion for Mexico after a trip there. Tacos made the way they do it there.
n10038019966.crowd: lunch and evening; the place is small

n2099385681.story: Elegant restaurant in Parcul Herăstrău, with a terrace facing the lake; for special occasions.

w277782378.story: Long-standing restaurant on Șoseaua Kiseleff, in an old villa with a large garden under the trees. Classic Romanian cuisine, good for a family meal or a more elegant evening.
w277782378.crowd: evenings; in the garden in summer

n1974128904.story: Tapas, paella and Spanish wine in the Dorobanți area, from the Alioli team.

w563922172.story: Food from Oltenia in huge portions at low prices, often recommended among the best cheap places in town.

n2634651950.story: The house in Berceni where Bacovia and his wife lived, the neighbourhood's first writer's museum: the family's furniture, manuscripts and photos, plus the flower garden.

n2634652142.story: Arghezi's house on Mărțișor street, a museum of the MNLR, surrounded by cherry and sour cherry trees planted by the poet; guided visits only.

n1768893912.story: Historic villa in Piața Lahovari with a restaurant and a quiet garden, hidden from the bustle of Magheru.
n1768893912.crowd: evenings; in the garden in summer

w495066823.story: Romanian restaurant across from Henri Coandă airport, with a covered, heated terrace plus a garden (up to 300 seats), so the terrace works in autumn and winter too; it also has a wine cellar.

n2800591014.story: Restaurant with a hotel and wine cellar on the Chitila–Mogoșoaia road, with Romanian and international food and a big terrace with a kids' playground.

c-carturesti-carusel.story: The white bookshop with spiralling balconies on Lipscani remains one of the must-stops on a walk through the centre. Entry is free, you look down on the whole "carousel" of books from above and step straight out into Centrul Vechi (Old Town).

n11068961012.story: Authentic Neapolitan pizza on Calea Victoriei, which quickly caught on despite being new.

n3779623861.story: Independent theatre space on Lânăriei street, known for shows on social and civic themes; in 2025 it ran the "Povești la Replika" nights, with theatre on Mondays and films on Tuesdays.

n11411704670.story: The only public institution dedicated to contemporary dance, with shows on Bulevardul Mărășești and in Sala Omnia; in November 2025 it held over 10 events.

c-centrul-vechi-lipscani.story: The pedestrian lanes between Lipscani, Smârdan and Covaci in Centrul Vechi (Old Town) are the classic starting point for a night out: dozens of bars, pubs and clubs a few steps from each other, street terraces and live music. In summer, on Fridays and Saturdays, it's the busiest nightlife area in town.
c-centrul-vechi-lipscani.crowd: Thursday–Saturday nights, until morning; busiest in summer

n5714624185.story: Café on Visarion where you paint your own ceramic mug or plate.

n9654423481.story: No-frills neighbourhood Vietnamese spot in Drumul Taberei: B365 called it "honest and delicious". Get the pho bo (39 lei) or the crispy duck with peanut sauce.

n849372378.story: Multiplex with 15 screens and over 2,800 seats in Sun Plaza, right by the Piața Sudului metro.

n3726839339.story: Multiplex with 14 screens in Mega Mall, including a 4DX screen where the seats move and you feel wind and water during the film.

n7079505521.story: The largest cinema in Romania, in AFI Cotroceni, with an IMAX screen for the big releases.

n9394387194.story: Multiplex with 14 screens in ParkLake, 3 of them VIP with big armchairs; easy to combine with a walk in Parcul IOR.

n849372410.story: Old cinema on Calea Moșilor, with 10-lei tickets and themed classic weekends (in October 2025: "Masters of Suspense", with Psycho and Rear Window).

n2468602231.story: Arthouse and documentary cinema in the Romanian Peasant Museum building on Kiseleff.

n849372350.story: One of the National Film Archive's cinemas, on Ion Câmpineanu street, with classics and retrospectives at low prices.

n849372318.story: The Romanian Cinematheque's historic hall on Eforiei street, with retrospectives, restored old films and festival screenings.

n7192898466.story: Cinema with 12 screens in Veranda Mall, with a Dolby Atmos screen and VIP screens with a private lounge; on Mondays tickets are much cheaper (17 lei in 2025).

n442896940.story: Small cinema with 7 screens, near the 1 Decembrie 1918 metro: good for a film without the crowds of the big malls.

w294724370.story: Multiplex with 13 screens in Băneasa Shopping City, with VIP screens and an Ultra screen with Dolby Atmos sound.

w23611484.story: The round, domed building in Parcul Circului, opened in 1961, hosts circus performances and international shows.

n7151190270.story: The first stand-up club in Bucharest, opened by comedians, at Bulevardul Dacia 99; shows every night, with big names and newcomers.

c-club-guesthouse.story: Bucharest's techno bunker since December 2010, in a former factory complex at Splaiul Unirii 160: Funktion-One sound system, sticker-covered walls and a "no phones" rule on the dance floor.
c-club-guesthouse.crowd: Wednesday–Saturday, especially Friday and Saturday nights

n9422684494.story: Club on Bălcescu, right in the centre: over 900 m², a big dance floor and quieter corners, themed parties at weekends and different nights during the week.

n2569444845.story: The club near Piața Rosetti, since 2013: lots of cheap beer, live folk on Tuesdays and Thursdays, karaoke on Wednesdays, club nights Friday–Saturday and old films on Sundays and Mondays. Student discounts available.

w23731450.story: Club with tennis courts and football pitches in Pipera, open daily from morning until midnight.

n13361797002.story: Coffee roastery with a café in the Dorobanți–Floreasca area.

c-coftale.story: The first specialty coffee shop in Bucharest (December 2012), in an old house with a garden on Ștefan Mihăileanu. Good for working too.

w700190532.story: One of the best-rated places in Sector 5 (Malcoci 2A, Rahova): 4.6 from 943 reviews.

c-combinatul-fondului-plastic.story: The art factory built between 1966 and 1972 by the Union of Visual Artists, now full of studios and independent galleries (Sector 1 Gallery, IOMO, The Institute); in 2025 it hosted exhibitions like "16M2" at Galeria SENAT.

n9643248317.story: Stand-up comedy club with shows almost every night (from 19, on Saturdays also from 16:30); good for a laugh with friends before the bar.

n1729617170.story: The home of indie and alternative music in the centre: two rooms with different music and an inner courtyard on Constantin Mille. In October 2026 it turned 18, with concerts by Liars and Lucy Kruger.
n1729617170.crowd: concerts during the week (check the schedule), parties Friday–Saturday after midnight

n13544497925.story: Known for its famous cookies, plus brunch, near Piața Amzei.

w1319614199.story: Outdoor ice rink next to AFI Cotroceni, open in winter, with skates for rent.

n10936959099.story: A project started in 2015 that brought young people back to the theatre: intimate shows, twice a night at 19:00 and 21:00, on Pache Protopopescu.

n7106605879.story: Turkish restaurant with meze, kebab and baklava, on Barbu Văcărescu.

w88337886.story: A 24-hectare old park on the shore of Lake Buftea, with the Știrbey Palace, the water tower designed by Anghel Saligny and an inner lake with ducks, geese and swans. There's a lakeside café and a restaurant. Open Friday–Sunday, 12–24, with a 50-lei voucher you spend at the restaurant. The Summer Well festival is held here in August.

n2918314870.story: The club in Mihăilești, praised for good music, energy and reasonable prices.

n7175227588.story: Small café on 11 Iunie street, close to Parcul Carol.

n450520681.story: Shawarma from Dristor is the benchmark all others are compared to; this is the spot next to Dristor metro.

n1731040881.story: Shaorma Dristor in Centrul Vechi (Old Town), on Franceză: the lifesaver after a night out.
n1731040881.crowd: late at night, after going out

n11463472510.story: Turkish and Lebanese restaurant on Decebal, from Ensar Duman's family of restaurants.
n11463472510.crowd: daily 11–24; good for a late dinner too

w402868001.story: Adventure park in the Balotești forest, with 14 tree-top courses, ziplines and climbing walls, plus ATVs, horse riding and paintball. Entry starts at around 25 lei, activities are paid separately and it closes when it rains.
w402868001.crowd: daily from 10:00 until sunset, especially weekends in the warm season

w402867798.story: Adventure park in the Balotești forest, with tree-top courses from easy to hard, a climbing wall, paintball and horse rides. You pay park entry, and each activity separately.

n1808662163.story: Sushi in a garden with a pond built specially for koi fish, on Știrbei Vodă. One of the best-rated sushi spots in town (4.9 from almost 2,000 votes on ialoc).
n1808662163.crowd: fills up in the evening and at weekends (about 50 seats), book ahead

n4554310490.story: Since 2011, one of the best Turkish restaurants in Bucharest, with decor that recalls Istanbul. It's 5 minutes from Timpuri Noi metro.

n6985316061.story: The French Institute's cinema on Bulevardul Dacia, named after actress Elvira Popescu, with European films and festivals.

n2587540738.story: Large bistro on Ion Brezoianu, at the edge of Cișmigiu, with European cuisine and a terrace.

n12109983201.story: Brunch bistro in the Tineretului area, on General Haralambie.

w550416782.story: Escape room on Bulevardul Dacia, for teams of 2 to 8 people, with one hour to break out.

n11295353657.story: Brunch spot in the centre, near Piața Amzei, featured in the 2025 brunch guides.

n10964569389.story: The alternative club Expirat now lives in Halele Carol, the former industrial halls next to Parcul Carol. In 2026 its stage hosted Omul cu Șobolani (29 years as a band) and Suie Paparude.
n10964569389.crowd: concert nights (usually from 21:30) and Friday–Saturday nights

w360140661.story: Adventure park in the Cernica forest, with tree-top courses colour-coded by difficulty and archery. The main draw is the long zipline over Lake Cernica.

w1449607814.story: Pub downstairs, club upstairs: on the ground floor you get pool, darts and wood-fired pizza, and upstairs is the 800-capacity hall that hosts some of the most important rock concerts in Bucharest.
w1449607814.crowd: daily until 5; follow the concert schedule

n3487482570.story: Climbing gym near Parcul Carol, with routes for all levels.

w202689090.story: Luxury club in Piața Presei Libere, with international DJs, shows and chill zones; tables are booked (standard from €500, VIP from €1,000, up to 9 people).
w202689090.crowd: Friday and Saturday nights, after midnight

w1173862898.story: The first farm park with domestic animals for children in Romania, opened in 2009 near Pantelimon: kids feed the animals, watch cows being milked, ride ponies and the zipline.

n7176366608.story: On Gabroveni since 2000, Fire is the students' club of Centrul Vechi (Old Town): rock, hip-hop and underground instead of commercial music, cheap beer and a covered atrium that opens onto Covaci.

n10856109721.story: A "botanical" bar on the 1st floor of Palatul Universul, open since 2016, with cocktails made from Eastern European ingredients: quince shrub, pollen liqueur, sunflower seeds. In 2025 it made the Top 500 Bars ranking.
n10856109721.crowd: any evening; ideal for the first cocktail of the night

n14058359291.story: Neapolitan pizza with a thin base and puffy crust, on Ion Mihalache.

n13104418691.story: Food hall in Hala Matache, rebuilt near Gara de Nord: several street food stalls under one roof, good when everyone wants something different.

n5290479000.story: One of the biggest clubs in town (about 850 m², opened in November 2010), with international DJs and concerts; the same complex holds Fratelli Lounge & Club and, in summer, Fratelli Social Club.

n2617153041.story: Brunch and coffee on Vasile Lascăr, near Piața Rosetti.

n10594078976.story: Chinese restaurant hidden on Intrarea Silistraru, in the west (Drumul Taberei–Militari); on Restograf's Chinese list and praised online as one of the best in town.

n2496044354.story: Italian restaurant on Bulevardul Decebal, a classic of the Alba Iulia area.

n1487149124.story: Hookah café in the passage at Calea Victoriei 16–20, with India-inspired decor and a large terrace; one of the best-rated cafés in town on Tripadvisor (4.9).

n10537965479.story: Super-creamy gelato with generous toppings and a classic Italian gelateria feel, on Calea Victoriei.

n7038740802.story: The purists' choice and Dristor's direct rival: quality meat and always-fresh ingredients, on Calea Floreasca.

n8004376949.story: Irish pub at Bulevardul Pipera 40B, with lots of whiskies and draught beer; rated 4.7, it has become a meeting spot in Pipera.

n6721487026.story: Italian gelateria often recommended by locals for its consistent quality; perfect on a stroll through Centrul Vechi (Old Town).

n11694509495.story: In Take Ionescu's former house, on Mircea Eliade street: garden terrace, bar with a fireplace, Romanian craft beer and the burger everyone praises.
n11694509495.crowd: Mon–Thu 16–23, Friday–Saturday until late; garden in summer

n10951615129.story: Bistro loved for its brunch and well-made bistro plates, near Piața Victoriei.

n2634651900.story: The garden founded in 1860 by Carol Davila: almost 18 hectares of plants from all over the world, shaded alleys and greenhouses.

c-gradina-botanica-dimitrie-brandza.story: The University of Bucharest's garden: paths among plants from around the world, a Japanese garden and greenhouses with palms and orchids, plus the Tropical Forest Pavilion. Tickets are 15 lei from 16 March to 15 October (08–20); in winter they cost 8 lei and hours are 09–15:30. The greenhouses have separate, shorter hours. UB students get in free.

w62743951.story: A small, charming garden from 1873, a stone's throw from Piața Romană, with a lake where ducks and swans live. Good for a short walk for two, which you can continue on the streets of beautiful villas in the Icoanei neighbourhood.

n12312753049.story: Restaurant with lots of greenery near Lake Snagov, for a quiet meal outside the city.

n1413464749.story: Garden café hidden behind the Cărturești Verona bookshop, a short walk from Piața Romană: shade, lemonade and books.

w369588750.story: The zoo in the Băneasa forest, with hundreds of animals and shaded paths.

n8565806982.story: Greek taverna with gyros, souvlaki and saganaki, on Mihai Bravu.

w1081931347.story: Founded in 1994 in a cellar at Calea Victoriei 120, it's the oldest jazz club in Romania since '89: weekly jazz, blues and funk concerts, plus the independent theatre LUNI.
w1081931347.crowd: concert nights; the jazz festival is in early June

n13763738501.story: Tea house in the Calea Călărașilor area, with teas from all over the world.

n7175225885.story: Specialty coffee shop in the Moșilor–Eminescu area.

n10111661681.story: Korean restaurant run by a Korean family, on Fabrica de Glucoză, 5 minutes from Pipera metro; it's also an Asian grocery. Try the Korean kimchi pizza or the tofu and seafood stew.

n2476458605.story: Beer hall in an interwar villa named after Elena Lupescu, King Carol II's famous mistress. Romanian food and beer on the terrace.

n2486324769.story: Inn built in 1808 by the Armenian merchant Manuc Bei; the negotiations for the 1812 Treaty of Bucharest were held here. In summer you eat in the inner courtyard, under the wooden galleries.
n2486324769.crowd: lunch or evening; courtyard in summer

n12165537279.story: Restaurant and pizzeria on Șoseaua Giurgiului in 1 Decembrie, very well rated (over 1,400 reviews on Restaurant Guru).

n769582150.story: Inn with Romanian food (the "Vlăsia" chicken and medallion, grilled lamb chops), a rustic dining room and terraces for hundreds of people; 3.7 from 891 reviews.

n12327311799.story: Cinema in Vitantis Shopping Center; in April 2025 it hosted the Classy Film Festival, with classics by Hitchcock, Kubrick and Fellini.

w809885097.story: Restaurant with a garden near the Arcul de Triumf, popular for weekend brunch.

n2994961690.story: Indian restaurant with tandoori, curries and naan, in the Moșilor area.

n3147680991.story: Hidden space on Doamna Chiajna that gives the stage to young artists (theatre, graphic art, music, writing); they also hold painting nights.

n849372311.story: The multiplex on the 2nd floor of București Mall, the first mall in Romania, opened in 1999.

n2486324774.story: Hookah and cocktail lounge in the passage at Calea Victoriei 16–20: coffee by day, hookah with friends by night.

n11891412206.story: Small Asian bistro in Piața Amzei, with Thai, Vietnamese and Indonesian food. The pad thai is the one people praise.
n11891412206.crowd: lunch and evening; the place is small

n7169802586.story: Neighbourhood pizzeria near Piața Muncii, with pizzaioli who worked in Naples, ingredients from Italy and a wood-fired oven.

n2839203559.story: Improv theatre founded in 2018, with shows in the attic at Comănița 9: no two nights are alike, and the audience gives suggestions.

n4574853189.story: Quiet tea house in Cotroceni, with many kinds of tea.

w298267725.story: Open since 18 September 2026, after decades of neglect: 3.4 ha with paths leading down to the water, running tracks and a beach area where you can sunbathe (swimming is forbidden). It also has pontoons for kayaks, boats and pedal boats.

n4408090991.story: Speakeasy-style cocktail bar on the ground floor of Magazinul Victoria, a building from 1928: piano, bicycles hanging on the walls, a DJ and, some nights, live music.

n12790924201.story: Opened in July 2020, it has 20 taps of Romanian and foreign craft beer, priced per 100 ml: you pick the glass size so you can taste more. The burgers go well with it.
n12790924201.crowd: Monday–Thursday from 17, Friday–Sunday from 12, until midnight

c-isan-thai-kitchen.story: Thai food from the Isan region (north-eastern Thailand), with ingredients mostly brought from there and a Thai chef. Maybe the best pad thai in town, says B365; also get the tom yum soup, laab and mango sticky rice.
c-isan-thai-kitchen.crowd: daily 13–23; fills up in the evening

n2939214402.story: Café-bistro on Calea Griviței, near Gara de Nord.

n10775253395.story: Korean table barbecue in Centrul Vechi (Old Town): you grill the meat yourself on the grill in the middle of the table.

w693861084.story: Lounge on the bank of the Dâmbovița, on Bulevardul Unirii, next to the National Library: hookah, nicely served food and a view of the river.

c-kaiamo.story: Chef Radu Ionescu's experimental Romanian cuisine: 3 Gault&Millau toques (15 points), seasonal tasting menus and over 200 wine labels. For a special evening.

n3602026798.story: Japanese restaurant in Dorobanți, with sushi and hot dishes, for a serious Japanese dinner.

n13011749006.story: Authentic, hearty Korean cooking in Dorobanți (Intrarea Tudor Ștefan 32). Start with mandu, the crispy dumplings with sweet-spicy sauce.

n8982367317.story: Specialty coffee shop on Bulevardul Octavian Goga.

n13483547254.story: Knafeh, the Levantine dessert with melted cheese and kadaif, served warm, on George Enescu.

n2526169547.story: Hookah lounge with Asian cuisine and furniture brought from Bali: over 100 tobacco flavours, sushi cut to order and a grill. A classic hookah is 150 lei.

c-komodo-lounge-old-town.story: The second Komodo, on Șelari in Centrul Vechi (Old Town): hookah, oysters and Ukrainian and Eastern European food.

n13781123201.story: Specialty coffee shop opened in 2025 in Cotroceni, on Doctor Joseph Lister.

n13522478476.story: The electronic music club that has made DJ Mag's top 100 clubs in the world several times; since 2012 it has been in a former cinema on Bulevardul Regina Elisabeta.

n718723997.story: Club on Sfânta Vineri with a concept brought from Berlin (the name means "house of culture"), room for 800 people and some of the lowest prices in the centre.

n12078943323.story: Thai restaurant since 2012, in the Domenii park, facing a quiet playground. Anne Ampawan and chef Songrit cook from Thai recipes: anything labelled "mild spicy" is actually hot.
n12078943323.crowd: lunch or dinner; book for the evening

n4521145291.story: Greek and Mediterranean restaurant on Louis Pasteur, in Cotroceni, with meat, fish and seafood.

n10266482712.story: Grill with "the best mici in the area", according to customers, at decent prices.

n13242491440.story: Bar & grill at Atomiștilor 250A in Măgurele, specialising in steaks and Romanian grill.

n10562319885.story: The neighbourhood restaurant in Berceni (Râul Mara 4), open since 2004, with Romanian and Italian food: pasta, steak, saramură.

n979620393.story: The La Mama chain, with home-style Romanian cooking and low prices, here in the Delea Veche–Muncii area.

n2503489527.story: The La Mama next to the Romanian Peasant Museum, with weavings and peasant objects on the walls. Filling Romanian food at student prices.

w941119947.story: Spanish-style fish and seafood, from the Alioli team, in Pipera.

n9505385222.story: Restaurant (with a hotel) at Bulevardul Voluntari 84C, among the best rated in town: 4.6 from 220 reviews on Restaurant Guru.

n11507864769.story: From the outside, the building on Popa Nan doesn't say much, but inside you feel like you're in a Greek taverna. The story began in 2010.

n3414077420.story: Reinterpreted Romanian cuisine in Centrul Vechi (Old Town), in a setting full of old objects collected from around the country. A good place to show friends from abroad how we eat.

c-lacul-snagov.story: From Snagov Sat, one-hour boat trips set off through the lake's nature reserve, with an audio guide. On the island in the middle is Snagov Monastery, from the 14th century, where legend says Vlad the Impaler is buried; boats can stop at its shore. At the leisure bases on the shore you can rent rowing boats, kayaks or SUPs.

c-lacul-snagov-snagov-parc.story: About 40 km from Bucharest, the Snagov Parc area has a beach on the peninsula with tree shade, pontoons and lakeside terraces, plus the Snagov forest for walks. At the Snagov Parc entrance there's a fee per car and per person.

n2360465919.story: Fish restaurant on the shore of the Căciulați pond, with a rustic wood-beamed dining room, terraces facing the lake (400 seats) and fishing pontoons.

n9775223451.story: Mediterranean restaurant in Ștefăneștii de Jos, with only homemade food, in a small, intimate space.

n10027946541.story: Laser tag arena in AFI Cotroceni: teams, sensor vests and a maze in semi-darkness.

n10608900638.story: The second LaserMaxx arena, in Vitantis Shopping Center, for team laser tag matches.

n7613023113.story: Gourmet kebab from Joseph Hadad's family: Levantine street food made with restaurant care, at the price of good shawarma.

n11078411661.story: The same gourmet Le Bab kebab, in Piața Charles de Gaulle, at the entrance to Herăstrău.

n13618974830.story: LiVU's eastern location, on Pache Protopopescu, from one of the first Vietnamese chains in Romania.

n5807532953.story: Rooftop on the 5th floor, on top of the Magazinul Victoria building on Lipscani, with views over the rooftops of Centrul Vechi (Old Town); in winter the tables sit in heated igloos.
n5807532953.crowd: at sunset, especially Thursday–Saturday; book the terrace early

c-london-club-biliard-snooker.story: Very central billiards club on Biserica Amzei, near Piața Romană: 17 pool tables, 2 snooker tables and private rooms.

n10984499946.story: Eclectic Mexican concept at Calea Victoriei 52, designed as a place to slow down: generous portions and bold flavours.

n11705012594.story: Dessert bar with choux and éclairs, in the centre, near the Athenaeum.

n11067430934.story: Chef Joseph Hadad's restaurant near the Athenaeum, with Mediterranean-Levantine cuisine.

n11462228739.story: Nepali restaurant named after the sacred Himalayan mountain Machhapuchhre: momo (steamed dumplings) and curries.

n8691238511.story: The Crângași lido, one of three affordable outdoor pools opened in Bucharest in 2026: room for 1,500 people, entry 85 lei on weekdays (60 after 16:00), 105 at weekends.

n11574150769.story: Lebanese restaurant run by chef Mohamad and his team, with over 15 years of Lebanese cooking. Get the shish kebab, tabbouleh or mixed grill.

n4395232476.story: Opened in 2015 in a building that was a police station for 60 years: film screenings with debates, workshops, concerts, exhibitions and parties.
n4395232476.crowd: on concert or party nights (schedule on iabilet)

n5435274421.story: Restaurant-lounge with distinctive decor in Complex LA (Amurgului 34), with a mixed menu (grill, burgers, pancakes); ranked 2nd of 149 places in Popești-Leordeni on Restaurant Guru.

n4866286521.story: The Romanian specialty coffee chain, here on Calea Floreasca.

n13247354036.story: Billiards club near Timpuri Noi, run by a former champion: Dynamic tables at 40 lei per hour, Spanish music and good food; the Masters Pool League is played here.

n11584831869.story: Tacos al pastor like in Mexico, near Piața Amzei.

n1008838657.story: Greek spot with fish and seafood (prawns, squid, octopus, sea bream), in an old boyar house near Calea Moșilor, with a terrace. Formerly Kostas.

n12074907530.story: In Agora Floreasca, one of the best places for breakfast or brunch in the area.

w891254538.story: Monastery built in 1638 by Matei Basarab near Lake Căldărușani, with centuries-old linden trees and a museum with icons painted by Nicolae Grigorescu.

w240611280.story: About 14 km from the city, Lake Cernica, over 300 hectares, is surrounded by forest, and the old monastery sits on islands in the lake. Good for a quiet walk; no music or barbecues on the monastery grounds.

w76904582.story: Founded by Michael the Brave in 1594; in 1985 the regime moved it 289 metres on rails and hid it behind apartment blocks.

w25511874.story: The monastery on the island in Lake Snagov, where legend says Vlad the Impaler is buried. Pairs well with a day at the lake and a boat trip.

w1169401746.story: One of the quietest and best-preserved monasteries near Bucharest, surrounded by Lacul Maicilor; easy to combine in one day with Snagov and Căldărușani.

w810258272.story: A huge church built at the end of the 18th century and abandoned before it was consecrated; its legend-filled ruins stand on the edge of Bucharest.

n6718728585.story: Coffee freshly roasted in Cluj, served on Regina Elisabeta, near Cișmigiu.

n9007779916.story: Greek restaurant with fish and seafood, in the Primăverii neighbourhood.

n7179103985.story: City Hall theatre on Bulevardul Mihai Eminescu, with comedies and contemporary plays in a mid-sized hall.

n13240848201.story: Mexican spot in Centrul Vechi (Old Town), on Gabroveni, with tacos and burritos made by a Mexican cook.
n13240848201.crowd: evenings, before going out in Centrul Vechi

n13564795451.story: Small specialty coffee shop in the Dorobanți area.

n5938945696.story: Sushi spot in the east of the city (Titan–Pantelimon area), on Gabriela Deleanu's list of recommended sushi places.

n10113765947.story: Neighbourhood burger joint with specialty coffee, beer and a cozy vibe; top rating on TripAdvisor.

n1731040985.story: Three floors on Gabroveni: live bands play in the basement, the ground floor is a pub with matches on screens, and upstairs there's karaoke every night from 21.

n849372344.story: The first cinema to bring 3D to Romania; it turned 20 in 2025 and has 11 screens in Plaza România.

n14219454376.story: Matcha bar near Piața Amzei, for anyone who wants something other than coffee.

n13094759001.story: Indian restaurant on Chile street, in Floreasca, focused on authentic flavour and beautifully plated dishes; among the best-rated Indian places in town on Tripadvisor.

n12288419303.story: Museum of illusions and interactive rooms in AFI Cotroceni, made for touching, trying and taking photos.

n2634652937.story: The home of collector Krikor Zambaccian, with paintings by Cezanne, Matisse and Renoir alongside Grigorescu and Luchian: a big collection in a small house.

w244848005.story: Private museum opened in 2018 on Bulevardul Primaverii, with Romanian art from after 1950 and temporary exhibitions.

n2634652010.story: A large military history museum near Gara de Nord, with tanks, cannons and planes on display, some out in the courtyard.

n4505417867.story: Sutu Palace, built in 1833–1835 in neo-Gothic style, hosted Bucharest's most famous balls; today it tells the story of the city.

n5146804838.story: A whole village of houses, mills and churches brought from all over Romania, on the shore of Lake Herăstrău. Its fairs (Mărțișor, Palm Sunday, Sânziene, the Bread Fair at the end of September) bring craftspeople and traditional food.

n2634652844.story: Named European Museum of the Year in 1996, with rooms designed as a story about the Romanian village; it also hosts fairs and a cinema in the same building.

n2634652277.story: The museum inside Cotroceni Palace, in the same complex as the Presidency; visits are by appointment and you need your ID with you.

n2634652837.story: In the former Royal Palace on Calea Victoriei: old and modern Romanian art, plus the European art gallery (Rembrandt, El Greco).

n2634652838.story: Contemporary art in the west wing of the Palace of the Parliament, open since 2004; go up to the top terrace for the view.

w23610985.story: The museum with the dioramas invented by Grigore Antipa: animals shown in their natural setting like in no other museum; fully modernised in 2011.

w220667665.story: A museum of inventors and machines in Parcul Carol, founded in 1909 by engineer Dimitrie Leonida, from old engines to vintage cars.

w38234390.story: The "Villa with Bells", built in 1905 by physician Nicolae Minovici in neo-Romanian style, houses a folk art collection next to Herăstrău Park.

n11222883615.story: Elegant Japanese restaurant with more than 40 dishes on the menu. For a big meal, get the Nadasan Set or the Sakura Set (56 pieces of sushi).
n11222883615.crowd: evenings; good for groups, book ahead

n2476489740.story: Indian restaurant on Mântuleasa with dishes from several regions of India; 4.7 on Tripadvisor, praised for tasty food and low prices.

n13017015601.story: Neapolitan pizza made from authentic recipes, close to Parcul Tineretului.

n12892532983.story: Hookah lounge on Mihai Bravu: specialty coffee by day, cocktails and hookah at night; reviews praise the good, cheap hookah (5.0 on Tripadvisor).

n11068954279.story: Bar on Calea Victoriei that makes its cocktails from Romanian spirits like tuica and palinca.

n13706065301.story: Over 30 Italian cocktails and Negroni variations, with Venetian cicchetti, in a retro art deco interior by Ukrainian architect Lisa Shinder; opens every day at 17:19 sharp.

n3067078344.story: Gaming pub on Tudor Vladimirescu: PC, console and board games, for an evening of drinks and play with friends.

n8524673437.story: One of the best-known Greek tavernas in Bucharest: gyros, souvlaki, bifteki, lamb chops, moussaka, grilled fish and seafood.

n10027946586.story: Nikos in the west, on Bd. Iuliu Maniu: a Greek taverna with gyros, souvlaki, bifteki and grilled fish.

n11463535891.story: Nikos near Piata Alba Iulia: the same big taverna menu, with gyros, souvlaki, moussaka and grilled fish.

n1416616482.story: Rooftop terrace on Smârdan with a retractable roof and a "secret garden"; after dinner it turns into a club with a DJ until morning.

n13781123302.story: Coffee roastery with a cafe in the Piata Iancului area.

n7090938385.story: On the 36th floor of Sky Tower, the tallest building in Bucharest: a panoramic view over the whole city, for dinner or a cocktail.

n13706030501.story: Chef Alex Petricean's restaurant (Gault&Millau Chef of the Year 2018), with a menu that takes you through the regions of Romania.

n9017905949.story: Hookah lounge at Foisorul de Foc, run by people with 8 years in the business: lots of flavours, cocktails and teas, plus board games and PlayStation in a separate room.

n11844514512.story: Restaurant with international food and a terrace at Padurea Mogosoaia 31-41 (Otopeni/Baneasa area), recommended on ialoc for going out with friends or kids; rated 5 from 17 votes.

n7826698274.story: Summer club on the shore of Lake Herăstrău, with Asian food with Peruvian influences and parties Wednesday to Sunday from 23; a dressed-to-impress crowd and prices to match.

n4261498192.story: Restaurant in Ferentari (Nasaud 99A) with American and Italian food at moderate prices; book on ialoc.

w79139872.story: Admiral Vasile Urseanu's villa, turned into an observatory: on clear evenings you look at the Moon and planets through a telescope, right in the centre.
w79139872.crowd: evenings, when the sky is clear

n13705806402.story: Speakeasy hidden behind the door of the former Post Office No. 1 on Matei Millo, with mailbox red in the decor and craft cocktails that change with the season.

n11068961018.story: Specialty coffee shop on Calea Victoriei.

n11331475896.story: Specialty coffee shop on Calea Mosilor.

w153452101.story: One of the biggest clubs in Bucharest, in Regie (Soseaua Orhideelor 1), with room for over 2,000 people; this is where big concerts and ticketed parties happen.
w153452101.crowd: Friday–Saturday nights and concerts (tickets on iabilet)

w23556393.story: The opera house near Podul Eroilor, opened in 1953, with opera and classical ballet all season.

w230389804.story: The south-east corner of Parcul Tineretului, with go-karts, bumper cars, a big wheel, roller coasters and a playground.

n7128123251.story: The northern Origo: a minimalist space, natural light, a short menu; loved by people working on laptops.

n3101709891.story: Probably the oldest specialty coffee shop in Bucharest, at Lipscani 9: the benchmark the others are compared to.

n7179021186.story: Coffee from seasonal harvests, roasted on carefully chosen profiles; this is the shop in the Aviatiei area.

w39349047.story: The Brancovenesc palace, with its loggia open to the lake, and the free-entry park are the favourite picnic spot 15 minutes from the city. In 2026 it also hosted festivals: Big Little Festival (August) and the first Always Forever, with about 6,000 people at sunset on the lakeshore.
w39349047.crowd: weekends, spring–autumn (come in the morning, it fills up fast); on summer weekends the stage on the main alley has theatre, music and films

c-palatul-parlamentului-tur-ghidat.story: The second-largest administrative building in the world, after the Pentagon; the guided tour enters from Strada Izvor (same entrance as MNAC) and you need your ID.

w38236017.story: The former home of the Ceausescu family, open to the public since 2016: gold-plated taps, a mosaic swimming pool and a private cinema.

w828136061.story: The palace on the shore of Lake Snagov can be visited with a ticket (70 lei adults, 60 lei pupils/students/pensioners).

r8321313.story: A park of about 85 ha in Titan, built around Lake Titan, which is split in two by the Liviu Rebreanu bridge and has five islands. The long waterside paths are great for walking, running or cycling.
r8321313.crowd: anytime, especially weekends and summer evenings

w13853540.story: A historic park on Filaret Hill: climb to the 48 m Mausoleum on the highest point, visit the "Dimitrie Leonida" Technical Museum right in the park, and stop by the lake with ducks and turtles. Concerts and events are held at the Arenele Romane in the park.
w13853540.crowd: weekend afternoons; evenings when there's an event at the Arene

w16291869.story: The historic park in the centre, with a lake: in summer you go out on a rowing boat or pedal boat (40 lei/hour in 2025), and in winter the lake becomes an open-air ice rink (2025–2026 season: 50 lei for an hour and a half, skates for rent on site).
w16291869.crowd: boats in summer, ice rink in winter (from December)

w395675082.story: A park of about 3 ha with rare decorative trees and shrubs on the shore of Lake Chitila. Walk, cycle or scoot along the shore (there's a bike lane), and there's a zip line for kids. Free entry, between 07 and 22.

w21802163.story: A renovated park with a lake crossed by a suspension bridge and a Japanese garden. There's a skatepark, basketball, football and tennis courts, ping-pong and chess tables, and an amphitheatre for shows.
w21802163.crowd: afternoons and evenings, in the warm season

w23611141.story: A shady park on Soseaua Kiseleff, between Piata Victoriei and the Arcul de Triumf, next to the Peasant Museum. In spring, Bucharest Street Food Festival moves onto the boulevard: in 2026, on 18–19 April, with dozens of food trucks, VAMA and Moonlight Breakfast.
w23611141.crowd: during festivals (April); otherwise, a daytime walk

r21298944.story: A new linear park built on a former railway line in Militari. It has an urban forest of about 900 trees, outdoor work pavilions with sockets and WiFi, a pumptrack, a bike lane, ping-pong and teqball tables, and hammocks.
r21298944.crowd: anytime; daytime if you want to work outdoors

w39349038.story: Around the Brancovenesc Palace there's a big park and lakeshore with free access: walk, have a picnic on the grass or grab a coffee on the terrace. You only pay to enter the museum (the palace, the kitchen house, the exhibitions): 15 lei adults, 8 lei pupils and students.

w88105780.story: A delta in the middle of the city, with reeds, ponds and birds you won't see in any other park. Walk the "Urban Biodiversity Trail" (2.3 km, about an hour) or cycle along the Belvedere dyke; in the warm season there are free guided tours with biologists and ornithologists. Open daily 07–21.
w88105780.crowd: mornings or towards sunset, spring to autumn

w88337000.story: Do the loop around Lake Herăstrău (almost 6 km), great for running, cycling or rollerblading, or take the little boat for a ride of about 25 minutes. At the Central Pier you can rent a rowing boat or pedal boat (12 lei/hour in 2025), and along the way you pass the Japanese Garden and the Rose Island.
w88337000.crowd: anytime; boats run daily in the warm season (spring–autumn)

w23652333.story: The park on Calea Rahovei, with playgrounds, fitness equipment, football and basketball courts, shady paths and a small fountain.

w23583220.story: A park on the shore of Lake Tei, with wide paths for walking and running. There are swans and ducks on the water, and right in the park there's a restaurant with a lake-view terrace.

w14360895.story: One of the biggest parks in the city: the wide path around the lake is made for running and cycling, you can rent a boat or pedal boat on the lake, and at the Bd. Gheorghe Sincai entrance there are bikes for rent. There are also sports courts and plenty of grass for a picnic.

r19937268.story: On Friday, Saturday and Sunday evenings, the fountains in Piata Unirii put on a show of about 45 minutes with water, lights and music; in 2026 the theme was famous films, with a few drone nights too. Free entry, but come a quarter of an hour early to get a good spot.
r19937268.crowd: Friday–Sunday evenings, May – early October (in September–October the show is at 20:00, in summer at 21:00–21:30)

c-parklake.story: For many young people in the east, the mall next to Parcul IOR is the meeting spot when it's rainy or cold: cinema, food court and, when the rain stops, you walk straight into the park.
c-parklake.crowd: all year, especially evenings and bad-weather days

w941119950.story: Italian restaurant in Pipera Plaza, praised for risotto, pasta and pizza; rated 4.5 from 106 reviews on Restaurant Guru.
w941119950.crowd: lunch with Pipera colleagues and evenings

c-padurea-baneasa.story: The forest on the northern edge of the city has three official bike trails: Blue (4 km, on paved paths), Yellow (6.5 km) and Red (7 km, on natural trails). There are picnic spots with tables and benches, and the Zoo is on the edge.

c-padurea-pustnicu.story: A wild forest on the shore of Lake Pasarea. "Ruta 10" is a 10 km bike trail on forest roads (there's also a 5 km version) starting from the Casa Pustnicu restaurant car park. There's also a lakeside path that's good for running, and a few barbecue spots. Muddy after rain.

w85952406.story: A reserve of about 1,470 ha near Lake Snagov, with old oaks and a rare patch of beech trees, unusual in the plains. The Snagov Foundation has marked trails: for example BI01, a 9.2 km loop on forest roads, marked with orange dots. In the reserve you may only walk on marked trails.

c-padurea-si-lacul-cernica.story: A large forest along Lake Cernica, a bird protection area since 2011, 15–20 km from the centre. It has wide trails, good for walking and cycling, picnic spots, and Cernica Monastery stands on the island in the lake.

n10630928720.story: Sichuan food cooked by a chef born and trained there. Order Kung Pao chicken or Mapo Tofu, as spicy as in China.

w23583384.story: A club with tennis, squash, a pool and spa near Lake Tei, named after former tennis player Dinu Pescariu.

w1224889723.story: Named after the famous Pho Thin soup from Hanoi; come for a hot beef pho near Obor.

n13917650801.story: Pho bar and Vietnamese street food on Mihai Eminescu.

n4466984690.story: A small family-run Vietnamese place on Bratianu near Unirii, with authentic cooking. B365 says it's "100% worth trying".
n4466984690.crowd: lunch and evenings; the place is small

n3647437509.story: A complex on the shore of Lake Cernica, with the a la carte restaurant Garuda and decks over the water.

c-piata-constitutiei.story: The huge square in front of the Palace of the Parliament fills up when something big is on: Street Food Festival and Bucharest Days in September (in 2026, Rudimental and video-mapping on the Palace), then the Christmas Market with a big wheel, a covered ice rink, over 130 stalls and concerts. Without an event it's just an empty square, so it's only worth it then.
c-piata-constitutiei.crowd: during events: Street Food Festival (early September), Bucharest Days (September), Christmas Market (late November – 28 December, especially evenings and weekends)

w281851047.story: The Lebanese place on Clucerului, near Piata 1 Mai: the menu has stayed almost unchanged for over 30 years.

w1168911692.story: A complex in Domnesti (Tudor Vladimirescu 309) with an adult pool (20×10 m) and a kids' pool, sun loungers, tennis courts and a gym.

n12252698101.story: Napoletinii Neapolitan pizza on Vasile Lascar, in the Gradina Icoanei area.

w408492998.story: The pizzeria in the centre of Buftea (Stirbei Voda 20A), with thin-crust pizza baked in a wood-fired oven.

n8154202096.story: On DN1 at Tancabesti, on the way to Lake Snagov: praised for the atmosphere, the staff and very good food.

n6464450486.story: An independent cultural hub in an interwar building near Piata Romana: intimate theatre upstairs, bar-cafe downstairs.
n6464450486.crowd: evenings, before or after a show

n4687665889.story: A restaurant open since 1991 in Chiajna, with Romanian food, a covered terrace and a playground for kids.

n7613023127.story: The metal bar in Centrul Vechi (Old Town) ("Rock 'n' Roll to Death!"): live concerts, metal karaoke, cheap beer and shots, and the sound carries out onto the terrace.
n7613023127.crowd: every evening from 17; Friday until 5, Saturday until 6

n648546126.story: Open since 2000 near Baba Novac: authentic Chinese recipes, well cooked, generous portions.

n2570329815.story: A classic pub near Piata Rosetti, with plenty of beer, a long whisky list and good music.

w438875605.story: The rock and metal club in Grozavesti: in autumn 2026 Danko Jones, Swallow the Sun and the Funk Rock Hotel festival bands (Suie Paparude, Moonlight Breakfast) play here.

n11582993011.story: Raw vegan restaurant in Floreasca: colourful raw dishes and no-bake desserts.

n13574655833.story: Specialty coffee shop in the Piata Romana area.

n10883984904.story: Game hall in Militari Shopping, with arcades and group games, open daily 10–22.

n11112041578.story: ReMatch game hall in Bucuresti Mall, with arcades and group games.

n8654444572.story: Restaurant with a pool in Ghermanesti (Sos. Ghermanesti 58A), 4.4 from 247 reviews; 43–110 lei per person.
n8654444572.crowd: summer, daytime at the pool; evenings for dinner

w986515791.story: A local landmark for authentic Romanian cooking in Buftea, on Strada Studioului.

n3265528742.story: Restaurant in Oraselul Copiilor (Calea Piscului), with pasta, traditional food, cocktails and seafood platters.

n5857522785.story: Grill restaurant with an international menu at Petre Ispirescu 9B (Rahova).

n3078194005.story: Casa Capsa, opened on Calea Victoriei in 1852, is where the Joffre cake was invented in 1920, in honour of the French marshal. Come for a slice of Joffre and a bit of history.

n1211033854.story: Elegant restaurant in Domnesti with Romanian and international food.

n3121977492.story: Chinese restaurant on Calea Dudesti, included by Restograf among the top Chinese places in Bucharest.

n5646198649.story: Restaurant in Mihailesti with Romanian and European food, a terrace and non-stop hours.

n4807344122.story: LiVU is one of the first Vietnamese restaurant chains in Romania; the one on Costache Negri is in the west, close to Cotroceni.

n2617494293.story: The first Chinese restaurant in Romania, opened in 1980. Food done by the book and pleasant evenings on the terrace.

w835097917.story: At the entrance to the Mogosoaia Palace park: a terrace and the "Domnita Balasa" hall in Brancovenesc style. Ideal after a walk through the palace gardens.

n13823565295.story: The second PengYou, on Occidentului near Victoriei: the same Sichuan cooking, with a Chinese chef, Kung Pao chicken and Mapo Tofu.

w837076386.story: Neighbourhood restaurant at Frumusani 8A, 4.6 from 414 Google reviews: varied menu, pleasant atmosphere, affordable prices.

w527662648.story: The restaurant by the pool of Stejarii Country Club (Tiriac's club), at Jandarmeriei 14A, across from Baneasa.

n4349316189.story: German beer hall at the Tecadra hotel in Pipera (Erou Iancu Nicolae 67A), with 70 seats, a summer terrace and a kids' corner.

w941063540.story: The villa in Baneasa Forest built in 1930 by architect Octav Doicescu, which in 1939 was one of the attractions of the New York World's Fair; the restaurant reopened in 2024 with an interwar feel.
w941063540.crowd: daily 12–24; weekend lunch, after a walk in the forest

n2468478918.story: The restaurant in the National Military Circle, the palace built in 1911–1923 on the site of the former Sarindar monastery. You eat in high-ceilinged halls or, in summer, in the garden.
n2468478918.crowd: lunch; summer evenings in the garden

n2994764233.story: Romanian restaurant a stone's throw from Cismigiu, with rustic decor and a homestyle menu: ciorba soups, sarmale, papanasi.

c-ruka-izakaya.story: Japanese izakaya in Agora Floreasca, with sharing plates: nigiri, sashimi, maki, teppanyaki, plus sake and Japanese highballs. Head chef Valentin Ungureanu runs the kitchen.
